::: {.chapter-lead}
This path guides you through an existing small decoder-only GPT: inspect its configuration and numerical building blocks, trace the Transformer block and assembled model, then run the generation loop. The tested reference code lives in [`src/llm_lab/foundations/`](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/tree/main/src/llm_lab/foundations); each of the five tours includes exercises with worked answers. You can use these tours to guide your own construction, but reading and running the reference is not evidence that you built it independently. Familiarity with Python and basic NumPy is useful; consult the linked concept pages for the mathematics and shapes as needed.
:::

::: {.callout-note .learning-outcomes collapse="true" title="Learning outcomes"}
By the end of this path, you will be able to:
- place the five modules of the reference code and their order of construction;
- run the reference code and its tests, then verify each available milestone's observable result (tensor shapes, causality, generation loop);
- explain why a randomly initialized GPT can demonstrate generation mechanics without learned language quality.
:::

## The code, in construction order

The tours follow a useful reading order, not a complete dependency list. For example, the block also uses `attention.py`, and generation imports the optional decoding filters. The source links show the actual imports; separating the minimal inference path from optional extensions remains future work.

1. **[The configuration](gpt-config-walkthrough.qmd)** ([`gpt_config.py`](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/src/llm_lab/foundations/gpt_config.py)): name and validate the model's dimensions before any computation.
2. **[The numerical building blocks](gpt-ops-walkthrough.qmd)** ([`gpt_ops.py`](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/src/llm_lab/foundations/gpt_ops.py)): initialization, linear projection, layer normalization, GELU.
3. **[The Transformer block](transformer-block-walkthrough.qmd)** ([`transformer_block.py`](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/src/llm_lab/foundations/transformer_block.py)): multi-head causal attention, MLP and residuals, in pre-LN order.
4. **[Model assembly](gpt-model-walkthrough.qmd)** ([`gpt.py`](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/src/llm_lab/foundations/gpt.py)): embeddings, stacked blocks, projection to logits.
5. **[Generation](gpt-generation-walkthrough.qmd)** ([`generate.py`](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/src/llm_lab/foundations/generate.py)): the autoregressive loop — pick a token, append it to the context, repeat.

## The model, assembled

After the setup below[^exec], run this complete example with `uv run --locked python example.py`. It uses a synthetic vocabulary and returns token IDs, not decoded text (see "Generate first, train later"):

```python
import numpy as np

from llm_lab.foundations import GPT, GPTConfig, generate

config = GPTConfig(
    vocab_size=50,       # V: embedding-table rows, logits per position
    context_length=32,   # T: positions processed in one pass
    embedding_dim=32,    # d: residual-stream width, divisible by num_heads
    num_heads=4,         # H: attention heads
    num_layers=2,        # stacked blocks
    mlp_hidden_dim=64,   # MLP hidden width
    seed=0,              # same seed, same parameters
)
model = GPT(config)
parameter_count = model.num_parameters()
assert parameter_count == 21426
print("Parameters:", parameter_count)

prompt = np.array([1, 2, 3])
greedy_ids = generate(model, prompt, max_new_tokens=8)
sampled_ids = generate(
    model, prompt, max_new_tokens=8, greedy=False,
    temperature=0.8, rng=np.random.default_rng(42),
)
print("Greedy IDs:", greedy_ids)
print("Sampled IDs:", sampled_ids)
```

For this configuration, the expected count is **21,426 parameters**. Each output contains the three prompt IDs followed by eight generated IDs; the two calls start from the same prompt. The reference code is pure NumPy (float64): readability first, speed later.

## Understand, build, deepen

At each milestone:

- **Understand** the mechanism: the linked concept page explains it — consult it when the question arises rather than beforehand.
- **Build and verify:** trace or implement the operation, make a prediction, and check it against the worked exercise and reference tests. The tours do not require you to write a full GPT from scratch.
- **Deepen** as needed: [tensors](tensors.qmd) and the [mathematical chain of training](mathematical-foundations.qmd) are references for shapes and gradients. Training also requires data, a loss and an update procedure; understanding gradients alone is not sufficient.
- **Practice:** try the questions in the relevant tour before opening its answers, or choose an available [exercise](exercises.qmd).

### Try a tour and check its evidence

Start with the [configuration exercise](gpt-config-walkthrough.qmd#exercises): predict whether the two width/head-count combinations are accepted, then compare your answer with the explanation. After the setup below, run `uv run --locked pytest --no-cov -q tests/unit/test_gpt_config.py` and inspect what the tests actually check. Continue with the exercises and linked tests in the [operations](gpt-ops-walkthrough.qmd#exercises), [block](transformer-block-walkthrough.qmd#exercises), [model](gpt-model-walkthrough.qmd#exercises), and [generation](gpt-generation-walkthrough.qmd#exercises) tours. `--no-cov` disables the whole-project coverage gate for this single-file run; the full test command below retains it. A passing test covers its stated cases; it does not establish independent construction or language quality.

## Generate, score and train: three uses of the same computation

The same predictive computation maps a context to a conditional distribution over the next token. This shared distribution serves three distinct uses: **generation** selects a token and feeds it back into the context; **scoring** measures the probability assigned to an observed token; **training** compares predictions with targets, computes a loss and its gradients, then updates parameters. Scoring and validation use fixed parameters: they do not trigger an optimizer step. The panorama details this [distinction between learning and inference](llm-overview.qmd).

The path explores generation first. A **randomly initialized** GPT has no learned language behavior to rely on: its shapes, causal mask and generation loop can be checked without demonstrating useful text. The example above returns IDs from a synthetic vocabulary; interpreting them as text would require a compatible tokenizer. This separation motivates the learning milestones: preparing [training examples](training-examples.qmd), optimizing a [loss](loss.qmd) with [gradients](gradients.qmd) — of which only the loss computations exist today (`losses.py`). The generation loop itself is detailed in [Generating text: inference step by step](generation.qmd).

## Build milestones

Before moving to the next step, produce or verify the indicated result; concept pages supply the mechanism, not proof that the code exists. The **G0–G9** identifiers are those of the [versioned build plan](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/docs/learning-path.md); **G2** (training data) is a parallel branch: required before training, not for generation.

| Step | What you build | Result to verify | To understand | Code status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 · G0. Define the model | The scope: a decoder-only GPT predicting the next token | Place this model among LLM families and Transformer architectures | [LLM panorama](llm-overview.qmd), [GPT and Transformer](transformer.qmd), [history](transformer-history.qmd) as context | Conceptual |
| 1 · G1. Prepare text input | Encoding and decoding a prompt with the tokenizer | Encode then decode a short text; identify the effect of special tokens and tokenizer version | [Text and data](text-data.qmd), [Unicode](unicode-text.qmd), [tokenization](tokenization-strategies.qmd) | Conceptual — no validated tokenizer pipeline |
| 2 · G3. Represent tokens | Embedding lookup and positional information | Trace shapes from `[B, L]` to `[B, L, D]` and name each axis | [Embedding space](embedding-space.qmd), [position](positional-encoding.qmd) | Reference — inside `gpt.py`; [tour: model](gpt-model-walkthrough.qmd) |
| 3 · G4. Compute attention | Q/K/V projections, scores, softmax and causal mask | With fixed parameters, append future tokens and compare the earlier-position logits | [Q/K/V](queries-keys-values.qmd), [attention](scaled-dot-product-attention.qmd), [causal masking](causal-masking.qmd) | Reference — `attention.py` (`scaled_dot_product_attention`, `causal_mask`, `softmax_with_temperature`); [tour: block](transformer-block-walkthrough.qmd) |
| 4 · G5. Assemble the GPT | Stacking the blocks: residuals, normalization, MLP and output projection | Trace dimensions through the model and check the parameter count (`model.num_parameters()`) | [Transformer](transformer.qmd), [tensors](tensors.qmd) as reference | Reference — [tours: block](transformer-block-walkthrough.qmd) and [model](gpt-model-walkthrough.qmd) |
| 5 · G6. Predict and select | Turning logits into a distribution, then the decoding rule | Distinguish logits from probabilities; explain greedy or sampled selection | [Logits](logits.qmd), [probabilities](probabilities.qmd), [generation step by step](generation.qmd) | Reference — inside `generate.py`; [tour: generation](gpt-generation-walkthrough.qmd) |
| 6 · G7. Generate before training | The full autoregressive loop, with random parameters | Run the loop on token IDs; check stopping and context window, without expecting learned language | [Generation step by step](generation.qmd) | Reference — [tour: generation](gpt-generation-walkthrough.qmd) |
| Data branch · G1b. Prepare the corpus and tokenizer | A traceable, eligible corpus, explicit splits, and a tokenizer that is fitted then frozen | Check provenance, deduplication, split hygiene and tokenizer consistency | [Corpus preparation](corpus-preparation.qmd); [tokenizer design/evaluation](tokenizer-design-evaluation.qmd) as optional depth | Conceptual plan available; complete loading, provenance, deduplication and split-audit pipeline not implemented |
| Data branch · G2. Create training examples | Context windows, shifted targets, batches and masks built from token streams | Build a window and its shifted target; test alignment, boundaries and leakage | [Training examples](training-examples.qmd); [tensors](tensors.qmd) as reference | Partial — sliding windows and shifted targets are tested in `training_examples.py`; full packing, padding, batching and masks remain to be built |
| 7 · G8. Train and validate | Compute loss on training targets, backpropagate and update parameters; measure validation separately with fixed parameters | Reproduce an update on a training batch; verify that a validation batch computes scores without calling the optimizer | [Cross-entropy](cross-entropy.qmd), [loss](loss.qmd), [gradients](gradients.qmd) | Partial — `losses.py` (`cross_entropy_from_logits`, `cross_entropy_gradient`); no complete loop, optimizer, automated validation runner or checkpoint |
| 8 · G9. Verify the implementation | Compare an implementation with a compatible reference (same architecture, tokenizer, weights and preprocessing) | Check configurations, parameters and numerical outputs with explicit tolerances; explain discrepancies | [GPT and Transformer](transformer.qmd), [generation](generation.qmd) | Criterion defined — no reference comparison of a trained checkpoint has been demonstrated yet |
| Cross-cutting · E1. Evaluate the task | Evaluate performance and limitations for a specific task on suitable data | Compare against a baseline under an explicit protocol; analyze errors, uncertainty and metric limitations | [Experimental evaluation](experimental-evaluation.qmd) | Method available — no complete evaluation of a trained GPT |

For the G4 causality check, inspect `test_prefix_invariance_future_tokens_do_not_change_earlier_logits` in the [model tests](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/tests/unit/test_gpt.py): it compares a prefix with a longer sequence under the same model. The NumPy reference has no train/eval mode switch. This test covers that prefix-extension case; it does not prove causality for every possible input.

For a first G2 check, take token IDs `[5, 6, 7, 8]` and a context length of 3: predict the input window and its one-token-shifted target. The [worked training-example lesson](training-examples.qmd) explains the convention; compare your answer with `test_corpus_of_context_length_plus_one_yields_one_window` in the [reference tests](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/tests/unit/test_training_examples.py). Run the file with `uv run --locked pytest --no-cov -q tests/unit/test_training_examples.py`. It does not test a complete corpus or data-splitting pipeline.

These criteria are learning objectives: an available page, a hand-checkable example, an automated test and a reproducible run are different levels of evidence.

## To continue

- [Exercises and practice](exercises.qmd): apply the milestones to exercises, separately from conceptual questions.
- [Versioned build plan](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/docs/learning-path.md): prerequisites, expected evidence, dependencies and validation criteria for each milestone.

[^exec]: Install Python 3.12+ and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), clone the repository (`git clone https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab.git` then `cd llm-lab`), and sync with `uv sync --locked --dev`. For the full test suite, also install the site-test dependencies with `uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -r docs/requirements-tokenizer-example.txt` and `uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -r docs/requirements-history-validation.txt`, then run `uv run --locked pytest`. Reinstall those requirements after a fresh sync, as explained in the [contributor guide](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). Save the example in a file named `example.py` at the repository root. The five tour test files are `test_gpt_config.py`, `test_gpt_ops.py`, `test_transformer_block.py`, `test_gpt.py` and `test_generate.py`; `test_attention.py`, `test_training_examples.py` and `test_losses.py` cover additional primitives.

::: {.callout-warning}
**An educational project, not industrial-scale training.** The small randomly initialized GPT makes transformations and errors inspectable; it does not reproduce the data volumes, compute resources or performance of a production LLM.
:::
